title: mysupermarketcompare.com: tiny profit, big traffic, numbers that do not agree
subject: UK insurance comparison site, live on Flippa (listing 12168548), asking $10,789
price_note: Price shown is the seller's asking price (multiples set to match it).
notes: The listing page and the search card disagree: card shows revenue $323 and profit $309 a month; the page shows revenue $383 and profit $285. This screen uses the card; ask which is right.
Revenue per 1,000 views is only about $2, so 152,122 views earn very little. Either the traffic count is wrong or most visitors never click through to the partner.
All revenue is affiliate commission from one partner company (single payer). The seller says 1 hour a week of work and a 95% margin.
Only Google Analytics is verified; the seller advertises 16 months of partner statements, which should be seen before any offer.

flags.risk: The one partner cuts or ends the commission
Traffic figure is overstated or bot-inflated
Profit really is lower than listed
flags.why: Two different profit numbers on the same listing

questions: Partner statements for all 16 months, matching bank deposits.
Which profit figure is right: $309 or $285, and why do they differ?
Traffic by country and by source for 12 months (Search Console export).
Why is revenue per 1,000 views so low: how many clicks go to the partner?
Is there a written agreement with the partner company, and does it transfer to a new owner?
Does the seller write or update the content, and who would after sale?
Any Google penalty, manual action or traffic drop in the last 12 months.
Do you hold FCA or affiliate-network permissions the site relies on? (UK comparison sites can need them.)
What costs sit between revenue and profit, who is paid?
Will the seller stay 60 days for hand-over?
